A1.justification: Both PDFs describe zip2zip, with matching core methods and experiments. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original token-efficiency, perplexity, downstream-task, translation, throughput, and ablation results in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds multilingual QA results and detailed compression statistics in Appendices H.2 and D.

M1.justification: The LZW vocabulary expansion, hyper-encoders, joint base/hypertoken prediction, caching, and training objectives remain unchanged. Renaming projection to unembedding and newly documenting document-level compression and the loss weight do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix H.2 adds multilingual QA and reasoning beyond the existing translation evaluation: TruthfulQA-2 in French, Spanish, Russian, Chinese, and Arabic; HellaSwag in four of these languages; and Winograd in three. Table 12 identifies unavailable combinations as NA. Existing training corpora and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged. Continued finetuning is renamed continued pretraining, and the added multilingual evaluation uses the same base-model and continued-training comparisons. Newly discussed methods such as Dynamic Vocab and H-Net are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Reported model identifiers receive limited revisions: the Apple M1 throughput row changes from Phi-3-4B to Phi-3.5-4B, and the 14B compute row changes from Phi-3.5-Medium to Phi-3-Medium. These are reported configuration changes, without evidence of reruns; the corresponding numerical values, context lengths, generation lengths, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix D adds quantitative analysis of the retained code, biomedical, and French examples, reporting sequence lengths, hypertoken counts, and compression ratios in Table 8. Table 9 also derives sequence-length reductions from existing token-efficiency results. The merge-size and hyper-encoder ablations and their training curves are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report approximately 0.02 bootstrapped uncertainty for the NLP accuracy results and identical bootstrapped translation deviations. V2 Table 11 combines existing translation means and deviations in one display. No new seed counts, repeated-run information, or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: V2 adds a substantial multilingual result block in Table 12: for example, French TruthfulQA-2 scores are 0.47, 0.42, and 0.41 for Base, continued pretraining, and zip2zip. Table 8 adds detailed example statistics, including code sequence compression from 344 to 265 tokens. Retained benchmark, throughput, and ablation values match; Table 9's 13–41% reductions are derived from existing measurements, not new performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 introduces entropy and cross-entropy invariance under lossless mappings in Theorem 2.1, with a proof in Appendix G. Appendix B.1 additionally introduces Proposition B.1 and a proof claiming an O(sqrt(N)) maximum merge-size bound. Neither theoretical result appears in v1; the existing training objectives and FLOPs derivation are retained.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains inference-time adaptive tokenization with inexpensive model adaptation. However, the abstract and introduction narrow sequence-length reduction claims from 20–60% to 15–40%, and the introduction reduces the maximum claimed end-to-end latency improvement from 60% to 40%.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces v1's inherent compression–quality trade-off explanation with an attribution to optimization difficulties under lossless compression, invoking the new invariance theorem. Section 3.5 also removes the malformed/repeated-number explanation for GSM8K degradation and explicitly treats tokenization-induced degradation as a hypothesis requiring validation. Appendix H.2 adds a domain-drift interpretation of multilingual results.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies document-level independent compression and the reconstruction-loss weight lambda = 0.1, explaining that extensive tuning was not performed. Its abstract explicitly reports released code and models rather than forthcoming code, while the introduction drops the vLLM compatibility claim. Most implementation, hardware, and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V1's claim to be the first inference-time dynamic-vocabulary method is replaced by identifying Dynamic Vocab as a close predecessor and distinguishing vocabulary construction and training. Section 4 and new Appendix A substantially expand positioning around dynamic embeddings and tokenization, including ZeTT, H-Net, SuperBPE, and FlexiTokens. The earlier Token Merging and Token Pooling discussion and references are removed.

P1.justification: V2 revises the title and substantially rewrites the abstract, contribution framing, related work, limitations, and conclusion. Terminology changes throughout from finetuning to continued pretraining and from projection to unembedding. Existing ablations are split into topic-specific appendices, technical details receive subsection structure, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: V2 adds the three-panel method illustration in Figure 2 and the lossless-mapping diagram in Figure 8, and redraws the architecture diagram as Figure 3. It merges the original accuracy and perplexity tables, combines translation means with uncertainties, adds compression and multilingual tables, and relocates the tokenizer-latency plot to the appendix. Existing empirical plots and output examples are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves calibration through narrower compression claims supported by Appendix D, acknowledgment of the closest dynamic-vocabulary predecessor, and additional multilingual evidence in Table 12. The explicit loss weight also improves reproducibility. These gains are limited by unchanged main empirical results and weaknesses in the added theory: entropy invariance for a transported distribution does not establish representability by the implemented model, so Section 5's optimization-only explanation overreaches. Appendix B.1 also does not justify summing substring occurrence lengths without establishing non-overlap.
